questions.question: What was the main aim of First Five Year Plan?
questions.solution: The focus of the First Five Year Plan was on the agricultural development of the country, of the Second was the industrial development of the country, of the third plan was to make the economy independent and of the Fourth Five Year Plan was growth with stability and achievement of self - reliance.

questions.question: "Detroit" is famous for which of the following Industries?
questions.solution: Detroit is the centre of the U.S. *automobile industry**,* as the "Big Three" auto manufacturers General Motors, Ford, and Chrysler are all headquartered in Metro Detroit.

questions.question: When does the problem of unfavourable balance of payments arise?
questions.solution: A balance of payments problem (also known as BOP deficit) means the country imports more goods, services and capital than it exports.

questions.question: Which one among the following formulates the fiscal policy in India?
questions.solution: Fiscal policy is formulated by the Ministry of Finance and it aims to set the limits of various deficits such as revenue deficit, budget deficit, fiscal deficit within the budget so as to drive the economy forward within the set limits of the deficits.

questions.question: When the first elected Lok Sabha came into existence in India?
questions.solution: The First Lok Sabha was constituted on 17 April 1952 after India's first general election. It lasted its full tenure of five years and was dissolved on 4 April 1957.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the most influential on the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: Indian Constitution is the largest written constitution in the world. It is a compilation of attributes taken over from a large number of sources. Yet, the foundations of the Indian Constitution are laid on major articles and clauses drawn from the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.question: To whom does the President address his resignation letter?
questions.solution: President of India will address his resignation letter to Vice President of India and in the absence of Vice President of India he will address it to the Chief Justice of India.

questions.question: Who determines the term and membership of the Central Council of Ministers?
questions.solution: President of India determines the term and membership of the Central Council of Ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister (Art. 75.1). It is for the Prime Minister to *determine* its size of the Central Council of Ministers according to the exigencies of the time and requirements of the situation.

questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment has the right to property been scrapped as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution: Right to property was scrapped as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment, 1978. It was instead made a constitutional right under Article 300A which states that ‘no person can be deprived of his property except by authority of law.’

questions.question: During which dynasty, Mahabalipuram temple was constructed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Pallava Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahabalipuram temple was constructed during the Pallava dynasty.
 
• The city of Mahabalipuram was founded by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I in the 7th century AD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Mahabalipuram (also known as Mamallapuram) temples were constructed during the Pallava dynasty in South India.
 
• Most of the temples in Mahabalipuram, including the famous Shore Temple, were built during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (also known as Mamalla) in the 7th century CE.
 
• His reign is considered a golden era for the Pallavas, marked by significant architectural and artistic achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Period:** 7th century CE.
 
• **Ruler:** Narasimhavarman II (630–668 CE).
 
• **Architecture:** The temples are known for their rock-cut architecture and intricate carvings, reflecting the early stages of Dravidian temple design.
 
• **Purpose:** The temples were built as monuments dedicated to Hindu deities, primarily Shiva and Vishnu, and also serve as a showcase of Pallava craftsmanship and maritime power.
 
• **Mahabalipuram is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site** due to its cultural and historical significance.

questions.question: Who among the following Governor - General introduced the policy of 'Doctrine of Lapse' during the British Administration?
questions.solution: The policy of Doctrine of lapse was introduced by Lord Dalhousie who was the British Governor - General of East India Company in India from 1848 to 1856.

questions.question: What is called the line on map joining places having equal pressure zones?
questions.solution:
**Isobar**

 
 
 
Is a line on a map connecting points having the same atmospheric pressure at a given time or on average over a given period

 
 
 

 
 
**Isohaline**

 
 
 
Is a line that joins points of equal salinity (saltiness or amount of salt dissolved in a body of water)

 
 
 

 
 
**Isotherm**

 
 
 
Is a line on a map or chart of the earth's surface connecting points having the same temperature at a given time or the same mean temperature for a given period

 
 
 

 
 
**Isohyet**

 
 
 
Is a line on a map connecting points having the same amount of rainfall in a given period

questions.solution: As one moves from the polar region towards the equator **the diversity** of plant and animal species “increases. The climate near the equator is more suitable in compare to the poles. The temperatures near the poles are not optimal for growth.

questions.question: Tracoma disease is related to which of the following organs?
questions.solution: Trachoma is an infectious disease caused by bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis. The infection causes a roughening of the inner surface of the eyelids.

questions.question: Which of the four blood groups, A, AB, B and O is called universal donor?
questions.solution: Blood group O can be given to persons of all types of blood group i.e. O, A, B and AB. Therefore a person with O type of blood group is called universal donor.

questions.question: Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of which of the following?
questions.solution: Vitamin A deficiency is a lack of vitamin A in blood and tissues. Nyctalopia (night blindness) is one of the first signs of VAD. Xerophthalmia, keratomalacia, and complete blindness can also occur since vitamin A has a major role in photo transduction.

questions.question: Seeds can best be preserved in which condition?
questions.solution: In general, most seeds stored in cool, dry conditions will survive longer than seeds stored in a wet, warm environment. The vigor and viability of seeds stored even at low temperatures declines over time.

questions.question: Rectifiers are used to convert __________.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__**:**

__
 
• A **rectifier **is a device that converts an alternating current into a direct current.
 
• A p-n junction can be used as a rectifier because it permits current in one direction only.

**EXPLANATION**__**:**

 
• A rectifier is an electrical device that **converts alternating current (AC), which periodically reverses direction, to direct current (DC), which flows in only one direction**. So option 4 is correct.

questions.question: When an object is transferred from Earth to Moon ________.
questions.solution:
• The mass of the object is **not changed** when it is transferred from Earth to Moon
 
• Only the **weight of the object decreases to its one-sixth** when transferred to Moon from Earth **due to the difference in gravity**
 
• The gravity of the moon is **one-sixth of the gravity** of the earth
 
• **Weight = mg,** (where ‘m**’** is the mass of the object and ‘**g’** is the acceleration due to gravity)

questions.question: If a computer has more than one processor then it is known as _________.
questions.solution: If a computer has more than one processor then it is known as is Multiprocessor, each processor have the capability of doing a task. If more than one processor is there then we can do multiple tasks at a time and it is called multitasking.

questions.question: What is full form of SMPS?
questions.solution: SMPS stands for Switched-Mode Power Supply. It is an electronic power supply that uses a switching regulator to convert electrical power efficiently

questions.question: Which among the following acids is used in Lead storage batteries?
questions.solution: The main active materials required to construct a lead acid battery are Lead peroxide (PbO₂), Sponge lead (Pb), and Dilute sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄).

questions.question: Which metal remains in liquid form at normal temperature?
questions.solution:
The **electrons in a mercury atom are bound more tightly than usual** to the nucleus as most other metals atoms **readily share their valence electrons** with other atoms.

Therefore, it takes **very little heat to overcome the weak binding** between mercury atoms.

Hence, mercury has a **low melting point**, is a **poor electrical and thermal conductor** and **doesn't form diatomic mercury molecules** in the gas phase

questions.question: Which of the following is not a noble gas?
questions.solution: Carbon is not a noble gas. Any of the gaseous elements Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, and Radon, occupying Group 0 (18) of the periodic table are noble gases as they are totally unreactive.

questions.question: Which element has maximum presence in the Sun?
questions.solution: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the Sun, accounting for over 90% of the atoms and over 70% of solar mass. The next most abundant element is helium, which accounts for almost just under 9% of the atoms and about 27% of the mass.

questions.question: Due to greenhouse effect __________.
questions.solution: Due to greenhouse effect temperature of earth is increasing. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) and other greenhouse gases act like a blanket, absorbing IR radiation and preventing it from escaping into outer space. There increased concentration leads to excess heating leading to temperature rise.

questions.question: Bringing Green Revolution to eastern India was a sub scheme of __________.

options.text: National Mission on Agriculture Extension and Technology

questions.solution: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI), was a sub-scheme of Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojna (RKVY) which was implemented in seven eastern states namely Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and eastern Uttar Pradesh from 2010-2011 to address the constraints limiting the productivity of rice based cropping systems.

questions.question: Who among the following was the inventor of long distance telephone?
questions.solution: Alexander Graham Bell was the inventor of long distance telephone.

questions.question: Which among the following is given to a player for instant energy?
questions.solution: Players are required to expend maximum energy in every game, and they must have the energy reserved to perform this task. Thus, carbohydrate intake is vital to getting the most out of their performance because when carbs are eaten they are eventually digested and broken down into smaller sugar molecules called glucose, which is the sole source of energy for the brain.

questions.question: Who among the following is the first Indian player to win a Grand Slam in Tennis?
questions.solution: Mahesh Shrinivas Bhupathi is a retired Indian professional tennis player. In 1997, he became the first Indian to win a Grand Slam tournament with Rika Hiraki.

questions.question: Apart from India, in which of the following country, Tamil is an official language?
questions.solution: Tamil is an official language of two countries: Sri Lanka and Singapore. It has official status in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu and the Indian Union Territory of Puducherry in India.

questions.question: Abhigyanshakuntalam' is a __________.
questions.solution: Abhigyanshakuntalam is a Sanskrit play by the ancient Indian poet Kalidasa, dramatizing the story of Shakuntala told in the epic Mahabharata.

questions.question: Black Sea Economic Cooperation Zone consists of ______ members.

questions.question: The ANZUS was signed in 1951 between _________.

questions.question: Palk Strait is between which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
• Palk Strait is a strait between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Mannar district of the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.
 
• It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with the Palk Bay and then with the Gulf of Mannar in the southwest.
